brief_item.title: IETF BMWG草案:AI推理服务网络架构基准测试方法学
brief_item.core_conclusion: 随LLM推理扩展到跨越数百上千加速器的解耦prefill/decode架构,互连架构成为决定TTFT、ITL与聚合吞吐的关键瓶颈,但缺乏厂商无关、可复现的以太网推理网络架构基准方法学。本草案定义四层KPI框架与九类测试,使RoCEv2与UET等传输栈具备可比性。
brief_item.mechanism: 定义四层KPI(主延迟:TTFT/ITL/TTFT_fabric等;主吞吐:TPS/Goodput/KV_BW等;架构层:KV_xfer延迟带宽、EP AllToAll、ECN/PFC等;健康指标)与九类测试(RDMA KV传输、PD解耦、MoE专家并行、拥塞管理、请求路由、延迟、吞吐、规模/弹性、稳定性)。遵循RFC 2544惯例(最少60秒试验,延迟最少20次重复),定义五种DUT/SUT配置(DUT-S/F/N/PD,SUT-E)以隔离不同测量范围。
brief_item.result: TTFT_fabric(KV Cache传输对TTFT的架构贡献)信息性参考目标<300ms P99(非通过/失败阈值);70B/FP16/4K上下文每请求KV Cache约1.34GB(约0.33MB/token);256专家top-2 MoE、EP=96、61层、30ms decode目标下低延迟分发路径需约2000次分发/s、约54GB/s聚合节点间带宽。所有KPI目标值均为非规范性信息参考点,非验收标准。
brief_item.boundary: 这是方法学/标准草案而非实验研究,定义测试流程但不报告任何具体厂商实现的实测结果;所有'目标'数值明确标注为非规范性信息参考点,非验收标准(BMWG章程排除验收准则);为Internet-Draft v00,无正式IETF地位,2026年8月过期,可能被更新/替换;参考文献节尚未填充,处于早期阶段。
brief_item.project_relevance: [判断]对TPN简报具有基础性意义:它直接定义了任何TPN式网络感知推理系统须据以评估的标准化KPI词汇(TTFT_fabric、KV_BW、KV_xfer延迟、EP AllToAll延迟)与测量方法学。TTFT_fabric分解正是量化网络侧相对纯GPU内存调度价值所需的指标;RDMA KV传输与PD解耦测试与跨节点KVCache传输兴趣直接对应。该草案实质上为整个TPN/推理网络空间建立了测量契约。

facts.title: IETF BMWG Draft: Benchmarking Methodology for AI Inference Serving Network Fabrics
facts.event_hint: IETF Internet-Draft (draft-calabria-bmwg-ai-fabric-inference-bench-00) defining vendor-independent KPI framework and test methodology for Ethernet-based AI inference network fabrics
facts.problem: As LLM inference scales to disaggregated prefill/decode architectures spanning hundreds or thousands of accelerators, the interconnect fabric becomes the critical bottleneck determining TTFT, inter-token latency (ITL), and aggregate throughput. However, there is no vendor-independent, reproducible benchmarking methodology for evaluating Ethernet-based inference network fabrics, making apples-to-apples comparison across NIC transport stacks (RoCEv2, UET) and fabric architectures impossible.
facts.mechanism: Defines a four-tier KPI framework and nine test categories for benchmarking Ethernet-based AI inference serving network fabrics under realistic workloads. (1) KPI tiers: Primary Latency KPIs (TTFT, ITL, TTFT_fabric, ITL_fabric, E2E_latency), Primary Throughput KPIs (TPS_input, TPS_output, TPS_per_GPU, Goodput, KV_BW, Request_Rate), Fabric-Level KPIs (KV_xfer_latency, KV_xfer_bandwidth, EP_alltoall_latency, EP_alltoall_bandwidth, Fabric_FCT, Buffer_utilization, ECN_marking_rate, PFC_frame_count, Link_utilization, Packet_drop_rate), and Fabric Health Indicators (switch CPU/memory, FEC errors, CRC errors, routing stability, NIC QP state, GPU-NIC PCIe BW). (2) Test categories: RDMA KV cache transfer (point-to-point throughput, latency, concurrent scaling, multi-tier storage), PD disaggregation (end-to-end TTFT decomposition, xPyD ratio optimization, heterogeneous parallelism, prefill queue depth), MoE expert parallelism (AllToAll throughput, normal vs low-latency dispatch, wide EP scaling, EP/KV contention), congestion management (ECN incast, PFC bursts, CC convergence, PFC storm resilience), request routing (KV-aware routing, prefix-aware cache hit, ECMP load balancing, JFI), latency (TTFT by prompt length, ITL tail, multi-tenant, congestion sensitivity), throughput (aggregate TPS, batch scaling, goodput under preemption), scale/autoscaling (cluster scale limits, autoscaling response, link failure convergence), and soak/stability (24-hour sustained load, memory leak detection, long-running stability). Tests follow RFC 2544 conventions: minimum 60-second trials, minimum 20 repetitions for latency (50 for burst). Defines five DUT/SUT configurations: DUT-S (single switch), DUT-F (complete fabric), DUT-N (NIC transport), DUT-PD (prefill-decode path), SUT-E (end-to-end system).

evidence.claim: The draft establishes a fabric-specific TTFT decomposition: TTFT_fabric is defined as the fabric contribution to TTFT (KV cache transfer latency) with an informational target of < 300 ms P99, measured NIC-to-NIC at DUT-PD.
evidence.condition: Informational reference target for interactive inference, not a pass/fail threshold

evidence.claim: For a 70B parameter model at FP16 with 4K context, KV cache is approximately 1.34 GB per request; at FP16 it is approximately 0.33 MB per token, establishing the scale of per-request fabric transfer demand.
evidence.value: 1.34 GB per request (70B, FP16, 4K context); ~0.33 MB per token

evidence.claim: Wide expert parallelism (e.g., 96-way EP across 12 nodes of 8 GPUs each) generates fine-grained, latency-sensitive inter-node traffic that contends with KV cache transfers on shared fabric links; for a 256-expert top-2 MoE model with 61 layers and 30 ms decode target, the Low-Latency Dispatch path requires ~2000 dispatches/s consuming ~54 GB/s aggregate inter-node bandwidth.
evidence.source_locator: Section 1 (Introduction) and Appendix D (MoE AllToAll Communication Pattern)
evidence.value: ~54 GB/s aggregate inter-node bandwidth for decode-phase MoE dispatch
evidence.baseline: 256 experts, top-2 routing, hidden_dim=7168, EP=96 across 12 nodes, 61 MoE layers, 30 ms decode target

evidence.claim: The methodology covers RDMA-based KV cache transfer (one-sided PUT/PUT-with-signal), MoE expert parallelism AllToAll communication, request routing and load balancing, congestion management under bursty inference traffic, and scale/soak testing, enabling comparison across RoCEv2 and UET transport stacks.

The draft defines five DUT/SUT configurations isolating different measurement scopes: DUT-S (single switch), DUT-F (complete fabric end-to-end), DUT-N (NIC RDMA transport), DUT-PD (prefill-decode path including NVLink/PCIe/fabric segments), and SUT-E (complete serving system for TTFT/ITL/TPS).

facts.evaluation_context: This is a methodology/standards document, not an experimental paper, so it defines test procedures rather than reporting measured results. Reference workload parameters: prompt lengths 128–16384 tokens; message sizes 64 KB–1 GB for KV transfer; EP group sizes 8–96 GPUs; xPyD ratios 1P11D through 11P1D; batch sizes 1–512; request rates 10–200 req/s; QP counts 1–128; background load 0–95% of fabric capacity. Tests target clusters up to 1024 nodes / 8192 GPUs. Transport stacks covered: RoCEv2 and UET (Ultra Ethernet Transport). The draft is version 00 of an IETF Internet-Draft (expires August 2026), companion to a training-fabric benchmarking draft. Authors: Fernando Calabria, Carlos Pignataro, Qin Wu, Giuseppe Fioccola.
facts.limitations: This is a standards/methodology draft, not an experimental study — it defines how to measure but does not report actual benchmark results from any specific vendor implementation. All numerical 'Target' values in the KPI tables (TTFT < 500 ms, ITL < 50 ms, TTFT_fabric < 300 ms, etc.) are explicitly marked NON-NORMATIVE informational reference points, not acceptance criteria. The draft states: 'Per the BMWG charter, the definition of acceptance criteria or performance requirements is explicitly outside the scope.' As an Internet-Draft (version 00), it has no formal IETF standing and may be updated, replaced, or obsoleted. It expires August 2026. [Inference] The draft does not yet include a populated References section (Sections 17.1 and 17.2 are empty), suggesting it is early-stage.
facts.project_relevance: This document is foundational for the TPN briefing. It directly defines the standardized KPI vocabulary (TTFT, ITL, TTFT_fabric, KV_BW, KV_xfer_latency, EP_alltoall_latency) and measurement methodology that any TPN-style network-aware inference system must be evaluated against. Key relevance points: (1) The TTFT_fabric decomposition (Section 4.1) provides the exact metric for quantifying the fabric's contribution to TTFT — directly answering the briefing question about network-side value vs pure GPU-memory scheduling. (2) The RDMA KV cache transfer benchmarks (Section 5) define how to measure cross-node KVCache transfer performance, which is central to the briefing's KVCache cross-node transfer interest. (3) The PD disaggregation tests (Section 6) formalize xPyD ratio optimization and TTFT decomposition including the T_transfer component. (4) The MoE AllToAll dispatch characterization (Section 7, Appendix D) quantifies the inter-node bandwidth demands of expert-parallel inference (~54 GB/s for decode), relevant to understanding total fabric load. (5) The DUT-PD configuration explicitly isolates the prefill-to-decode data path including NVLink, PCIe, and fabric segments — enabling CXL/disaggregated memory and DPU/SmartNIC offload relevance assessment. This draft effectively establishes the measurement contract for the entire TPN/inference-network space.
